C1. Site overview

Site metadata and product citations are taken from the FLUXNET snapshot used by the generator.

C2. Data coverage

The heat map shows, for each site and year, the share of half hours with NEE_VUT_REF_QC == 0. Gray cells indicate years outside a site’s record or a missing QC column in its file.

Best measured-data coverage was 58.2% at MN-Nkh in 2016.

C3. Summary statistics

The tables summarize the half-hourly records. For P_F, the mean is the mean annual precipitation total; its minimum and maximum are half-hourly values. Missing percentages use all half hours in each site’s file. Variables absent from a file are shown as 100% missing.

C4. Time series

Daily values are the mean of the available half-hourly records for each calendar day, multiplied by 1.0378 to convert to g C m⁻² d⁻¹. The panels share one y-axis scale; gaps remain where the half-hourly variables are missing.

Daily aggregation check: for FI-Hyy, the converted HH daily means agree with FLUXMET_DD; the largest absolute difference across the three fluxes is 0.0011 g C m⁻² d⁻¹.

C5. Diurnal cycles

The x-axis is local standard time (no daylight-saving shift), grouped by hour 0–23. Meteorological seasons are reversed for sites south of the equator.

C6. Your reading

Energy balance

The fit and scatter use only half hours where both H and LE have QC flag 0 and all four energy variables are present. The fit uses every qualifying row; the displayed scatter is thinned to at most 20,000 points for readability.

The energy-balance figure will appear here after scripts/c1.py has been run with the tower data.

At US-WCr, the fitted slope was 0.694 from 190,803 measured half hours.

Using negative annual NEE as net uptake and years with at least 90% valid daily values, FI-Hyy had the largest mean annual sink at -220.0 g C m⁻² yr⁻¹ across 26 years. I defined seasonal-cycle size as the range of the 12 calendar-month mean daily NEE values; DE-Geb had the largest range at 6.2 g C m⁻² d⁻¹. A surprising data limitation is that US-WCr (1999–2025) has no usable values for the plotted NEE, GPP, or RECO series. Among non-missing NEE QC flags, the gap-filled fraction (QC > 0) ranged from 49.1% at MN-Nkh to 69.7% at DE-Geb. Among non-missing QC flags, the measured fraction (QC = 0) was highest at MN-Nkh (50.9%) and lowest at DE-Geb (30.3%) among sites with QC data. The annual sink comparison uses NEE_VUT_REF, while gap-filled percentages exclude intervals with missing QC flags.
